messages.content: @Andrew Wingate - What would you call the type of diagram which is used to show the mechanical parameters of something which is used by people to design cases and such?
It would just be a mechanical drawing.

I mean, there are other words you can use, but it's unnecessary. 
If you're designing for something else to fit in/on/around you can apply GD&T stuff that basically outlines some tolerances on the part they may not have. 
Other stuff like form/fit/function, but again, a lot of this is just embedded into a mechanical drawing if you desire.
@Tim 'mithro' Ansell are there any online-fpgas with radios attached to them?

Not at the moment -- but I separately have set up a bunch of RPi hardware which have SDR systems connected to them -- some which have FPGAs. I think it was/is a Pluto, Kraden SDR, RTL-SDR and soon a xsdr
Ah, hence the adapter to put the xsdr on a Pi HAT.
Does your Pluto setup intend for the bitstream to be overwritten or is it just IQ receive via Pluto IIO APIs?
I have no idea!
I think I broke the pluto while working on trying to get my 433mhz to wifi bridges working
Ok I will stay tuned!
@storborg - I'd most certainly appreciate any help with improving fpgas.online

I think there is some basic infrastructure stuff that's broken at the moment?

I tried, as advised by the docs (https://github.com/CarlFK/pici/wiki/Getting-Started) to pick an FPGA, e.g. this one:
https://welland.fpgas.online/fpgas/pi38.html

I built an Arty A7-35T bitstream locally and tried to upload it with the form in the top right. I get a 413 Request Entity Too Large served by nginx, on a 2.1MB .bit file.

So then I tried to connect via ssh using the `ssh -p 23822 pi@welland.fpgas.online` instruction. No dice, doesn't look like anything is listening on that port.

Then I tried clicking the "Reset" button, which I presume is supposed to power cycle the PoE port. It did update the websocket messages to indicate the control socket was cycled, but it didn't affect the state of the LEDs in the video feed at all, and ssh login isn't any more successful.

messages.content: Claude is claiming that it has fixed a bunch of the problems you identified. In theory I have an end-to-end test which shows it works now (by using the system like a human) but I haven't had a chance to test it myself manually.
It's broken in new and different ways now

ssh to the individual pis doesn't seem to be listening, or maybe the ports are wrong. Uploading a bitstream directly with the web form sometimes throws a 500 and sometimes succeeds, but never seems to actually do anything.
Got a test bitstream?
I haven't fixed the direct ssh connection yet -- does the webssh terminal work for you?
Here's an Arty 35 bitstream that should make the LEDs do something noticeable and distinct on the video stream
The webssh terminal sort of works, although it seems to sometimes not load. I guess I can curl from somewhere else via webssh.
If I do that and flash the board manually via openFPGALoader, it completes successfully, but I don't see anything on the video feed.
I tried on a different board (https://welland.fpgas.online/fpgas/pi37.html) and it seems to be working, although the view of the LEDs is really blurry.

It would be kind of cool if the Pi could just read LED or Pmod state directly and show it on the web interface. I presume there is some wiring between the Pmods on the boards and the Pis that I could use to do that.
I assume the reason this is more reliable on ps1 and less reliable on welland is that ps1 doesn't use the per-port VLAN configuration?

Honestly, I kinda feel like you could forego the camera feed entirely and just show a bunch of outputs of different types that could be driven directly from the FPGA.

I could imagine the 'thumbnail' of the board instance showing whether or not it's running a bitstream / has a user interacting with the pi, the filename of the bitstream that's running, and a country flag to indicate the remote user that loaded the bitstream.
